summary: Untested backups are hopes. This app has no restore drill: Postgres is down and the owner-scoped store is in-process. A tired rm -rf analogue here is dropping the memory dict or pointing REDIS_URL at production.
evidence: GitLab had dumps, snapshots, and a replica that was the thing being wiped. We will not say 'we have backups.' Verified restore would be: take a pg_dump, restore into a throwaway DB, run SELECT on a known short_code, time it. That drill has not been run because localhost:5432 is not serving — same class of honesty as GitLab publishing that dumps had been failing.

The in-process links dict and TTL cache die on process restart with no snapshot. That is worse than GitLab's 6-hour Azure lag: we would lose all Module 04–06 links. Mitigation when DB is up: persist created_by + long_url, and never use a replica as the only backup.

Tired-operator control: destructive ops need a second check (wrong-server rm). Our analogue is not running docker stop / DROP TABLE without an explicit user request; cache invalidate is a key delete, not a flushall.
